body_markdown:
Ford just released a new special-edition package for the Mustang GTD that pays homage to Henry Ford’s fabled race car, “Sweepstakes.” It’s called the Mustang GTD 1901, and it’s a tribute to a pivotal year in Ford’s history.


Ford


In 1901, Henry Ford was still just a struggling entrepreneur, hoping to make it big in the automotive industry. To garner some investor interest in what he had going on, he took his latest car, called “Sweepstakes,” and entered it in a car race in Grosse Pointe, Michigan. Ford ended up winning, investors took notice, and, well, 125 years later, the[Mustang GTD](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ford-mustang-gtd-competition-nurburgring-time/) has a striking new paint color.


Ford


Ford


The GTD 1901 will replace the[Spirit of America](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ford-celebrates-good-ol-american-ingenuity-with-revised-mustang-gtd-spirit-of-america/) package, which was a nod to Craig Breedlove, another man obsessed with speed and racing. For an undisclosed premium over the normal $325K-ish Mustang GTD, the 1901 gets a striking red and black exterior treatment. Ford calls the paint color Royal Red, and it looks sublime in these photos. Inside, there’s a matching Mahogany Red leather interior that gives this track missile an almost luxury-like feel.


Ford


Ford


Because the GTD 1901 is celebrating a race victory, Ford’s offering the Performance Package as standard on this version. The Performance Pack focuses on aerodynamic improvements, including a large splitter and dive planes up front, an active rear wing with a drag-reduction system, and underbody flaps to improve airflow.


This leather looks tasty in here, but we also think it would look just as good in an F-150.


Ford


Alongside this new package, the rest of the[GTD lineup](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-mustang-gtd-first-drive-true-to-its-roots/) receives a handful of updates for the 2028 model year. The optional magnesium wheels, which shave roughly 50 lbs of unsprung weight over the standard aluminum wheels, are available in two new colors: Black or Luster Nickel. The 3D-printed paddle shifters and the shift ring on the eight-speed dual-clutch transmission have been redesigned. Inside, the cabin gets a bit ritzier with a full-grain leather wrap for the instrument panel, door panels, and center console. There are new painted stripe options for the exterior, and an updated color package for the GTD Liquid Carbon trim with flashy teal accents.


Ford
